body: What was the bug? Anything I can help fix? I can't see the linked ticket.
author: devongovett

body: It wasn't a bug, it's just that lightningcss is more restrictive than swc_css, so technically invalid syntax that swc_css was handling gracefully was failing hard with lightningcss. What we'll probably end up doing for now is enabling lightningcss behind a flag instead of doing a direct swap. Ideally, we'll be able to make lightningcss the default and remove swc_css when we release the next major version.
author: padmaia

body: What was the syntax error in particular? Not sure if you tried already, but there's also an [error recovery](https://lightningcss.dev/docs.html#error-recovery) option which is more lenient in parsing. Maybe that could also help.
author: devongovett

body: Oh interesting... I'm not sure if the team tried that already either, I'll dig and get back to you.

mkdir foo

node index.js

@ijjk I can't edit labels myself. This PR is not about documentation (though I added some documentation to reflect the code change). It is about changing Next.js `route.ts` type definition to allow custom exports. Which is not currently possible.

Also the discussion (https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/55140) hasn't been picked up by anybody, do you know if I could mention someone who could be interested in having a look at my proposal ?

body:
@theo-lubert 

> Some cases require to export some info: data, configs, types for the client, etc...

Wouldn't you want these `/lib` type of logic in a separate directory? 

> could enable a lot of nice features (especially around type inference imo).

Is it possible to elaborate on this (versus having like a separate `types.ts` file)?

> Next.js currently forces us to create separate files

Is the issue because the thought is you _can't_ export multiple methods in a Route Handler?
author: samcx
theo-lubert

body: Hi @samcx @leerob  what can we do to make this happen ? or at least move in any direction ? A year is a long time. It really is a small change. Thx a lot
author: theo-lubert

body: We don't have precedent for this type of change. As this problem is solvable by placing the other exports within a separate file (the `/lib` solution), I'd suggest that we don't proceed with this change.
author: wyattjoh

body:
Moving to `/lib` doesn't solve this imo, as the relevant data still is in `route.ts` (we want to infer types and data from it)

Best case scenario, you can move the code in another file colocated in the same dir.
This means `route.ts` basically becomes a one liner that export the methods form another file. This duplication doesn't feel right to me. And making `route.ts` more extensible is a good way to solve this.

`_` prefix seems resonable, as its usually meaning is "ignore this"

Do you see any risk in allowing us to extend `route.ts` this way ?
author: theo-lubert

body: Adding sever-only helps avoid file misuse. If all i18n dictionaries leak to the browser, bundle size will get huge. The import helps to prevent this.
author: kachkaev

body: It looks like the redirect functions are hardcoded to `307`/`308` redirects. How do you do `301`/`302`/`303` redirects then?
author: GabenGar

body:
> Why does Next.js use 307 and 308? Traditionally a 302 was used for a temporary redirect, and a 301 for a permanent redirect, but many browsers changed the request method of the redirect to GET, regardless of the original method. For example, if the browser made a request to POST /v1/users which returned status code 302 with location /v2/users, the subsequent request might be GET /v2/users instead of the expected POST /v2/users. Next.js uses the 307 temporary redirect, and 308 permanent redirect status codes to explicitly preserve the request method used.

From the docs 🙏
author: leerob

body: Yeah but there might be use cases for when you want to change the method to `GET` and `301`/`302`/`303` are go-to SEO redirects (SEO doesn't operate outside of `GET` requests anyway). I have a suspicion some search engines can choke on `307`/`308` by assuming these are invalid codes.

> FYI I have removed `__NEXT_PRIVATE_PREBUNDLED_REACT` in #55762

`__NEXT_PRIVATE_PREBUNDLED_REACT` is the env I have encountered with `worker_threads`, yet many more env used internally by Next.js need to be passed down to build/route workers (`__NEXT_PRIVATE_CROSSORIGIN`, `__NEXT_ANALYTICS_ID`, etc.).

`pnpm test-start test/production/ci-missing-typescript-deps/index.test.ts` one failed because there's throwing a new error introduced before 27.0.0. 

https://github.com/jestjs/jest/blob/6c83c0f91d219771d6c0c2ce32231053cae322b5/packages/jest-worker/src/workers/ChildProcessWorker.ts#L185-L189
author: huozhi

body:
> `pnpm test-start test/production/ci-missing-typescript-deps/index.test.ts` one failed because there's throwing a new error introduced before 27.0.0.
> 
> https://github.com/jestjs/jest/blob/6c83c0f91d219771d6c0c2ce32231053cae322b5/packages/jest-worker/src/workers/ChildProcessWorker.ts#L185-L189

The real cause of the CI failure is the inproper handling of the worker exiting.

I've fixed that in [`7bd1a95` (#55257)](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/55257/commits/7bd1a95cc326a7d1ebe9fd9eb681d577e7bdef1d).
